evidence: Names motives of European integration after 1945
Puts the main treaties on a timeline
Explains what makes the EU a community of values
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard the EU called a "peace project", could they explain where the idea comes from?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on EU basics from Kl. 6
Integration in the context of the Cold War

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: EU Institutions and Law-Making
topics.description: Pupils describe the tasks of the European Parliament, the Council of the EU, the European Commission, the European Council and the Court of Justice, and outline the ordinary legislative procedure and the difference between regulations and directives.
evidence: Names the main EU institutions and their tasks
Outlines the ordinary legislative procedure
Distinguishes regulations from directives with an example
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that a new EU rule requires the same charger for all phones, could they explain which institutions decided it and how?

prerequisites.reason: Institutions developed with integration
Comparison with national legislation

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: The Single Market
topics.description: Pupils explain the four freedoms of the single market (goods, services, capital, persons), and discuss opportunities and challenges for consumers, companies and workers.
evidence: Names the four freedoms with everyday examples
Explains advantages of the single market for consumers
Discusses challenges such as wage competition
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wanted to do an apprenticeship in Austria, could they explain which EU freedom allows this and what else the single market changes?

prerequisites.reason: The single market is a core of integration
Market basics

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: The Euro and Monetary Union
topics.description: Pupils describe the features of the Economic and Monetary Union – the euro, the European Central Bank, convergence criteria and the Stability and Growth Pact – and discuss its advantages and the experience of the euro crisis.
evidence: Names advantages of a common currency
Explains the convergence criteria
Describes the euro crisis and its causes in outline
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} travelled from Germany to Italy and Croatia, could they explain why they can pay with the same money and what holds the euro together?

prerequisites.reason: Monetary union builds on the single market
Functions of money

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Democratic Legitimacy of the EU
topics.nameDe: Demokratische Legitimation und Zukunft der EU
topics.description: Students evaluate the decision-making powers of EU institutions with regard to democratic legitimacy ("democratic deficit"), the effect of EU law on national legislation, and discuss future models of integration (federation, intergovernmental cooperation, differentiated integration).
evidence: Explains the debate on the democratic deficit
Explains the primacy of EU law with a case
Discusses future models of integration
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard someone say "Brussels decides everything and nobody elected them", could they evaluate this claim?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on Sek I knowledge of the institutions
Democratic theory as criterion

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Universal Human Rights
topics.description: Pupils explain the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), the idea of universality and indivisibility, the European Convention on Human Rights, and assess human rights violations and the ways to protect rights.
evidence: Explains the universality of human rights
Names institutions protecting human rights (UN, European Court of Human Rights)
Assesses a current human rights violation and possible responses
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read a report by Amnesty International, could they explain which human rights are violated and how they could be protected?

prerequisites.reason: Children's rights as a human-rights convention
The historical origin of human rights

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: The United Nations
topics.description: Pupils describe the aims and main organs of the UN (General Assembly, Security Council with veto, Secretary-General, International Court of Justice), peacekeeping missions, and judge possibilities and limits of the UN.
evidence: Names the aims of the UN Charter
Explains the role of the Security Council and the veto
Judges why the UN often fails to stop wars
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that the Security Council could not agree on a war, could they explain how the veto works and why this matters?

prerequisites.reason: Human rights are a UN aim
The UN was founded after the Second World War

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Analysing International Conflicts
topics.description: Pupils analyse an international conflict, crisis or war with a fixed scheme – actors, causes, interests, course, options for resolution – and distinguish types of conflicts (interstate war, civil war, terrorism, hybrid war).
evidence: Applies a conflict analysis scheme to a current conflict
Distinguishes types of armed conflict
Develops and evaluates options for conflict resolution
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} followed a war in the news, could they analyse the actors, causes and interests involved?

prerequisites.reason: Conflict resolution in everyday life
International actors in conflicts

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: NATO, the Bundeswehr and German Security
topics.description: Pupils describe NATO's tasks and the alliance case (Art. 5), the role of the Bundeswehr as a "parliamentary army" (deployment needs the Bundestag), compulsory military service debates and Germany's security policy after 2022.
evidence: Explains collective defence under Article 5
Explains why Bundeswehr deployments abroad need the Bundestag's approval
Discusses current debates on security and military service
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard a debate about bringing back compulsory military service, could they explain the role of the Bundeswehr and NATO?

prerequisites.reason: Collective security as context
Parliament decides on deployments

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Free Trade and Protectionism
topics.description: Pupils describe the growing interconnection of world trade, the aims of actors (WTO, states, companies, NGOs), the features of free trade and protectionism (tariffs, quotas, subsidies) and judge free-trade agreements.
evidence: Explains tariffs and other protectionist measures
Describes the role of the WTO
Judges the effects of a free-trade agreement on different groups
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that a country raised tariffs on imported cars, could they explain who wins and who loses?

prerequisites.reason: Globalisation of trade
Free trade within the EU

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Theories of International Trade
topics.description: Students explain theories of international trade – absolute and comparative advantage (Smith, Ricardo), arguments for protection (infant industry, security) – and analyse current trade conflicts and the limits of national economic policy.
evidence: Explains comparative advantage with a numerical example
Explains arguments for protectionism
Discusses the limits of national economic policy under globalisation
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why a country that can produce everything more cheaply still gains from trade, could they explain comparative advantage?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on Sek I trade policy

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Concepts of Peace and Conflict Research
topics.description: Students explain concepts of peace and conflict research – negative and positive peace, structural violence (Galtung), causes of war – and discuss how different ideas of peace can be implemented.
evidence: Distinguishes negative and positive peace
Explains structural violence with an example
Discusses strategies of peacebuilding
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked whether a ceasefire means peace, could they answer with Galtung's concepts?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on Sek I conflict analysis

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Theories of International Relations
topics.nameDe: Theorien internationaler Beziehungen: Realismus und Institutionalismus
topics.description: Students explain realism (states, power, security dilemma) and institutionalism (cooperation, international institutions, interdependence), and use them to analyse international politics and the role of the UN.
evidence: Explains the core assumptions of realism and institutionalism
Explains the security dilemma
Analyses a current conflict with both theories
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} analysed NATO enlargement, could they explain how a realist and an institutionalist would interpret it differently?

prerequisites.reason: Peace research and IR theory
The UN as an institution

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: German Foreign and Security Policy
topics.nameDe: Deutsche Außen- und Sicherheitspolitik in NATO und EU
topics.description: Students evaluate goals, possibilities and limits of German foreign and security policy within NATO and the EU's Common Foreign and Security Policy, including the "Zeitenwende" after 2022 and the debate on Germany's international responsibility.
evidence: Explains the instruments of the EU's Common Foreign and Security Policy
Describes the shift in German security policy after 2022
Evaluates Germany's international role with criteria
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard the term "Zeitenwende", could they explain what changed in German security policy and evaluate the change?

prerequisites.reason: Theories frame foreign-policy analysis
Builds on Sek I security policy

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Social Contract Theories
topics.description: Students compare the social contract theories of Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau – state of nature, image of humans, purpose and form of the state – and trace their influence on modern constitutions.
evidence: Compares the state of nature and image of humans in Hobbes and Locke
Explains Rousseau's idea of the general will
Traces an element of the Grundgesetz back to a contract theory
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} were asked why people should obey a state at all, could they compare the answers of Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau?

prerequisites.reason: Enlightenment ideas met in history
The Grundgesetz as application

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Separation of Powers
topics.description: Students explain Montesquieu's theory of separation of powers and analyse its horizontal, vertical (federalism) and temporal forms as well as the "interlocking" of government and parliamentary majority in Germany.
evidence: Explains Montesquieu's argument for separating powers
Distinguishes horizontal, vertical and temporal separation
Analyses where powers interlock in the German parliamentary system
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard that ministers are also members of the Bundestag, could they discuss whether this contradicts the separation of powers?

prerequisites.reason: Part of Enlightenment political theory
Applied to the German system

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Pluralist and Identitarian Democracy
topics.description: Students compare the pluralist theory of democracy (Fraenkel: competition of interests, consensus on rules, common good a posteriori) with identitarian concepts (Rousseau, common good a priori), and judge which theory underlies the Grundgesetz.
evidence: Explains the core ideas of pluralist theory
Contrasts it with the identitarian concept of the common good
Judges risks of the identitarian model with historical examples
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} heard a politician claim to know "the will of the people", could they analyse this with the contrast between pluralist and identitarian democracy?

prerequisites.reason: Rousseau's general will is the basis of identitarian theory
Interest groups in pluralism

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Deliberative Democracy
topics.description: Students explain the theory of deliberative democracy (Habermas: public discourse, the "unforced force of the better argument") and evaluate deliberative formats such as citizens' assemblies.
evidence: Explains the ideal of deliberation
Compares deliberative with pluralist democracy
Evaluates a citizens' assembly as a deliberative format
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} read about a citizens' assembly on climate policy, could they evaluate it with the theory of deliberative democracy?

prerequisites.reason: Deliberative theory responds to pluralism
Public sphere and media

topics.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
topics.name: Rawls' Theory of Justice
topics.description: Students explain Rawls' theory of justice – original position, veil of ignorance, principle of equal liberty and difference principle – and use it to evaluate social-policy measures, comparing it with libertarian criticism.
evidence: Explains the veil of ignorance and the two principles
Applies the difference principle to a social-policy measure
Compares Rawls with a libertarian position
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} had to design a tax system without knowing whether they would be rich or poor, could they explain what Rawls would expect them to choose?

prerequisites.reason: Principles of justice applied to inequality
Rawls renews contract theory

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to interpret written sources, pictures and political cartoons step by step, to compare different perspectives on the same event and to separate factual from value judgements.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Textquellen, Bilder und Karikaturen schrittweise zu interpretieren, Perspektiven auf dasselbe Ereignis zu vergleichen und Sach- von Werturteilen zu unterscheiden.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to look critically at history in films, computer games and museums and to tell evidence from invention.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Geschichte in Filmen, Computerspielen und Museen kritisch zu betrachten und Belegtes von Erfundenem zu unterscheiden.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how Germany remembers its past – memorials, concentration-camp memorial sites, Stolpersteine and days of remembrance – and why.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie in Deutschland an die Vergangenheit erinnert wird – Denkmäler, KZ-Gedenkstätten, Stolpersteine und Gedenktage – und warum.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how emperors, popes and princes ruled in the Middle Ages, what life was like in medieval towns, and about the crusades, Jewish communities and long-distance trade.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie Kaiser, Päpste und Fürsten im Mittelalter herrschten, wie man in der mittelalterlichen Stadt lebte und was es mit Kreuzzügen, jüdischen Gemeinden und Fernhandel auf sich hatte.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about the Renaissance and printing, the voyages of discovery and conquest of America, the Reformation, witch hunts, the Thirty Years' War and absolutism.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt über Renaissance und Buchdruck, Entdeckungsfahrten und Eroberung Amerikas, Reformation, Hexenverfolgung, den Dreißigjährigen Krieg und den Absolutismus.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how the Enlightenment led to the American and French Revolutions and human rights, how Napoleon reshaped Germany and why the revolution of 1848/49 failed.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie die Aufklärung zur Amerikanischen und Französischen Revolution und zu den Menschenrechten führte, wie Napoleon Deutschland veränderte und warum die Revolution von 1848/49 scheiterte.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how industrialisation changed work and life, how people answered the social question, and how the German Empire was founded in 1871 and governed.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie die Industrialisierung Arbeit und Leben veränderte, welche Antworten es auf die Soziale Frage gab und wie das Kaiserreich 1871 entstand und regiert wurde.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about European imperialism and German colonial rule, the causes and character of the First World War, the turning point of 1917 and the Treaty of Versailles.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt über den europäischen Imperialismus und die deutsche Kolonialherrschaft, Ursachen und Charakter des Ersten Weltkriegs, das Epochenjahr 1917 und den Versailler Vertrag.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how Germany's first democracy began in 1918/19, what its constitution looked like, how it survived crises and why it collapsed by 1933.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie Deutschlands erste Demokratie 1918/19 entstand, wie ihre Verfassung aussah, wie sie Krisen überstand und warum sie bis 1933 scheiterte.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how the Nazis seized power, how ideology, propaganda and terror shaped life, about the persecution and murder of Jews and other groups in the Holocaust, the Second World War and resistance.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie die Nationalsozialisten die Macht übernahmen, wie Ideologie, Propaganda und Terror den Alltag prägten, über Verfolgung und Ermordung der Juden und anderer Gruppen im Holocaust, den Zweiten Weltkrieg und den Widerstand.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how Germany was divided after 1945, how the Cold War shaped the world, how life differed in the FRG and the GDR, and how the Peaceful Revolution led to reunification in 1990.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie Deutschland nach 1945 geteilt wurde, wie der Kalte Krieg die Welt prägte, wie unterschiedlich das Leben in BRD und DDR war und wie die Friedliche Revolution 1990 zur Einheit führte.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to criticise sources at Abitur level, to form reasoned historical judgements, to discuss historians' controversies and to reflect on how historical knowledge is made.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Quellen auf Abiturniveau kritisch zu interpretieren, begründete historische Urteile zu fällen, Kontroversen der Geschichtswissenschaft zu erörtern und über die Entstehung historischen Wissens nachzudenken.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your teenager is evaluating how both German states and united Germany have dealt with the Nazi past and how remembrance culture developed.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind bewertet, wie beide deutsche Staaten und das vereinte Deutschland mit der NS-Vergangenheit umgingen und wie sich die Erinnerungskultur entwickelte.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your teenager is working with the concepts of nation, nationalism and empire, analysing modernisation around 1900 and the history of German Jews and modern antisemitism.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind arbeitet mit den Begriffen Nation, Nationalismus und Imperium, analysiert Modernisierung um 1900 und die Geschichte deutscher Juden und des modernen Antisemitismus.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your teenager is comparing struggles for participation from Athens to 1848, discussing explanations of National Socialism and comparing twentieth-century dictatorships.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind vergleicht Kämpfe um Teilhabe von Athen bis 1848, erörtert Erklärungsansätze zum Nationalsozialismus und vergleicht Diktaturen des 20. Jahrhunderts.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your teenager is studying China and Russia as empires, colonialism and its legacies, and decolonisation in a global perspective.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschäftigt sich mit China und Russland als Imperien, mit dem Kolonialismus und seinen Folgen sowie mit der Dekolonisation in globaler Perspektive.

clusters.subject: Geschichte
clusters.summary: Your teenager is analysing the end of the post-war boom after 1973 and the structural change in East and West Germany.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind analysiert das Ende des Nachkriegsbooms nach 1973 und den Strukturwandel in Ost- und Westdeutschland.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to analyse complex thematic maps and to read and draw geographical diagrams and statistics.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, komplexe thematische Karten auszuwerten und geographische Diagramme und Statistiken zu lesen und zu erstellen.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to work with web-based GIS and to show geographical processes as causal diagrams.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, mit WebGIS zu arbeiten und geographische Prozesse als Wirkungsgefüge darzustellen.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to analyse a region from many materials in Abitur style and to reach a reasoned judgement.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, einen Raum anhand vieler Materialien im Stil der Abiturprüfung zu analysieren und begründet zu beurteilen.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how plate tectonics explains volcanoes, earthquakes and tsunamis, and why people still live in hazard zones.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie die Plattentektonik Vulkane, Erdbeben und Tsunamis erklärt und warum Menschen trotzdem in Risikoräumen leben.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is studying the Earth as a system of interacting geofactors and analysing natural hazards, risk and vulnerability.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind betrachtet die Erde als System zusammenwirkender Geofaktoren und analysiert Naturrisiken, Vulnerabilität und Katastrophenvorsorge.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the climate zones of the Earth and how the trade-wind circulation creates rainy and dry seasons in the tropics.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Klimazonen der Erde kennen und wie der Passatkreislauf Regen- und Trockenzeiten in den Tropen erzeugt.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how the greenhouse effect causes climate change, what its consequences are and how we can protect the climate and adapt.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie der Treibhauseffekt den Klimawandel verursacht, welche Folgen er hat und wie Klimaschutz und Klimaanpassung gelingen können.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is analysing climate scenarios, tipping points and questions of climate justice between rich and poor countries.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind analysiert Klimaszenarien, Kipppunkte und Fragen der Klimagerechtigkeit zwischen reichen und armen Ländern.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the landscape zones of the Earth and how people farm in rainforests, savannas and deserts – and the damage caused by misuse.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Landschaftszonen der Erde kennen und wie Menschen im Regenwald, in der Savanne und in Trockenräumen wirtschaften – und welche Schäden falsche Nutzung anrichtet.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is analysing how agriculture changes in a globalised world and weighing food security against sustainability.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind analysiert den Wandel der Landwirtschaft in einer globalisierten Welt und wägt Ernährungssicherung gegen Nachhaltigkeit ab.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how the global water cycle works and why fresh water is unevenly available.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie der globale Wasserkreislauf funktioniert und warum Süßwasser ungleich verteilt ist.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about water scarcity, virtual water and conflicts over water, and how the oceans are used and protected.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt über Wasserknappheit, virtuelles Wasser und Wasserkonflikte sowie über Nutzung und Schutz der Meere.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how economies shift towards services, why location factors change, and what long-haul tourism means for developing regions.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie sich Wirtschaft zum Dienstleistungssektor verschiebt, warum sich Standortfaktoren wandeln und was Ferntourismus für Entwicklungsräume bedeutet.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is analysing structural change in industrial regions, models of tourism development and, in the advanced course, central place theory.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind analysiert den Strukturwandel von Industrieregionen, Modelle der touristischen Entwicklung und im Leistungskurs das System der Zentralen Orte.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how cities are structured and why cities worldwide – especially megacities in the Global South – are growing so fast.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie Städte gegliedert sind und warum Städte weltweit – besonders Megastädte im Globalen Süden – so schnell wachsen.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is analysing the Central European city model, suburbanisation, segregation and gentrification, and concepts for sustainable, climate-resilient cities.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind analysiert das Modell der mitteleuropäischen Stadt, Suburbanisierung, Segregation und Gentrifizierung sowie Konzepte für nachhaltige, klimaresiliente Städte.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how the world population grows, how to read population pyramids and the demographic transition model, why people migrate, and how Germany is ageing.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie die Weltbevölkerung wächst, wie man Bevölkerungsdiagramme und das Modell des demographischen Übergangs liest, warum Menschen wandern und wie Deutschland altert.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is discussing the carrying capacity of the Earth and how to secure food for a growing population.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind erörtert die Tragfähigkeit der Erde und die Sicherung der Ernährung für eine wachsende Bevölkerung.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how development is measured, why countries and regions develop unequally and how development cooperation and fair trade try to help.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie Entwicklung gemessen wird, warum sich Länder und Regionen ungleich entwickeln und wie Entwicklungszusammenarbeit und Fairer Handel helfen wollen.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is comparing development theories such as modernisation and dependency theory in the advanced course.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind vergleicht im Leistungskurs Entwicklungstheorien wie Modernisierungs- und Dependenztheorie.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning what globalisation is, how global production chains and global cities work and how digitalisation changes places.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, was Globalisierung ist, wie globale Produktionsketten und Global Cities funktionieren und wie Digitalisierung Räume verändert.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is analysing transnational economic alliances in a multipolar world.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind analysiert transnationale Wirtschaftsbündnisse in einer multipolaren Welt.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to compare fossil and renewable energy sources and their effects on landscapes and the climate.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, fossile und erneuerbare Energieträger und ihre Folgen für Landschaft und Klima zu vergleichen.

clusters.subject: Erdkunde
clusters.summary: Your teenager is working with the sustainability model and evaluating the transformation of energy supply, including Germany's Energiewende.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind arbeitet mit dem Leitbild der Nachhaltigkeit und bewertet die Transformation der Energieversorgung, auch die deutsche Energiewende.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the principles of the Grundgesetz, how basic rights protect and where they end, what the rule of law means, and how juvenile criminal law works.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Verfassungsprinzipien des Grundgesetzes kennen, wie Grundrechte schützen und wo sie enden, was Rechtsstaat bedeutet und wie das Jugendstrafrecht funktioniert.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how Germany's parliamentary system works: Bundestag and government, how laws are made with the Bundesrat, and the role of the Federal Constitutional Court.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie das parlamentarische Regierungssystem funktioniert: Bundestag und Bundesregierung, Gesetzgebung mit dem Bundesrat und die Rolle des Bundesverfassungsgerichts.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how citizens can take part in politics beyond elections – petitions, initiatives and demonstrations.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie man sich über Wahlen hinaus politisch beteiligen kann – mit Petitionen, Bürgerinitiativen und Demonstrationen.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how Bundestag elections work, what parties and interest groups do, and how democracy protects itself against extremism.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie die Bundestagswahl funktioniert, was Parteien und Verbände tun und wie sich die Demokratie gegen Extremismus schützt.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your teenager is weighing representative against direct democracy and analysing populism and threats to democracy.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind wägt repräsentative und direkte Demokratie gegeneinander ab und analysiert Populismus und Gefährdungen der Demokratie.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning why free media matter for democracy and how to recognise disinformation and the effects of algorithms.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, warum freie Medien für die Demokratie wichtig sind und wie man Desinformation und die Wirkung von Algorithmen erkennt.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your teenager is analysing media logic, agenda setting and how politics is staged for the media.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind analysiert Medienlogik, Agenda-Setting und die Inszenierung von Politik in den Medien.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning their rights as a consumer, how to plan a budget and avoid debt, and how online shops use personal data.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt seine Rechte als Verbraucher, wie man ein Budget plant und Schulden vermeidet und wie Onlinehändler persönliche Daten nutzen.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to compare ways of saving and investing by return, risk and liquidity, and how interest and inflation affect savings.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Spar- und Anlageformen nach Rendite, Risiko und Verfügbarkeit zu vergleichen und wie Zinsen und Inflation das Ersparte beeinflussen.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how households, firms, banks and the state are connected in the circular flow of the economy.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie Haushalte, Unternehmen, Banken und Staat im Wirtschaftskreislauf verbunden sind.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the principles of the social market economy, how taxes finance the state, and what inflation is.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Prinzipien der Sozialen Marktwirtschaft, wie Steuern den Staat finanzieren und was Inflation ist.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your teenager is using economic models – market equilibrium, market failure, business cycle – and comparing economic-policy concepts and the ECB's monetary policy.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind arbeitet mit ökonomischen Modellen – Marktgleichgewicht, Marktversagen, Konjunktur – und vergleicht wirtschaftspolitische Konzeptionen und die Geldpolitik der EZB.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is exploring their strengths and career options, including dual vocational training and university.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind erkundet seine Stärken und berufliche Wege, darunter duale Ausbildung und Studium.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how firms work and are founded, how unions and employers negotiate wages, and how employees have a say at work.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie Unternehmen funktionieren und gegründet werden, wie Gewerkschaften und Arbeitgeber Löhne aushandeln und wie Beschäftigte im Betrieb mitbestimmen.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning how Germany's social insurance works, how poverty is measured and fought, and the rules on migration, asylum and integration.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, wie die Sozialversicherung funktioniert, wie Armut gemessen und bekämpft wird und welche Regeln für Migration, Asyl und Integration gelten.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your teenager is studying sociology – socialisation, roles and identity, social inequality and models of social structure – and comparing welfare-state models.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschäftigt sich mit Soziologie – Sozialisation, Rolle und Identität, soziale Ungleichheit und Sozialstrukturmodelle – und vergleicht Modelle des Wohlfahrtsstaats.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning why Europe united after 1945, how EU institutions make laws, and what the single market and the euro mean in everyday life.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, warum sich Europa nach 1945 einigte, wie die EU-Institutionen Gesetze machen und was Binnenmarkt und Euro im Alltag bedeuten.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your teenager is evaluating the democratic legitimacy of the EU and discussing its future.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind bewertet die demokratische Legitimation der EU und diskutiert ihre Zukunft.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about human rights, the United Nations, NATO and the Bundeswehr, how to analyse international conflicts and the debate on free trade.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt über Menschenrechte, die Vereinten Nationen, NATO und Bundeswehr, wie man internationale Konflikte analysiert und über die Debatte um Freihandel.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your teenager is working with theories of peace, international relations and trade, and in the advanced course evaluating German foreign and security policy.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind arbeitet mit Theorien zu Frieden, internationalen Beziehungen und Außenhandel und bewertet im Leistungskurs die deutsche Außen- und Sicherheitspolitik.

clusters.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
clusters.summary: Your teenager is reading political theory – Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, Montesquieu, theories of democracy and, in the advanced course, Habermas and Rawls.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschäftigt sich mit politischer Theorie – Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, Montesquieu, Demokratietheorien und im Leistungskurs Habermas und Rawls.
